solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Support a struggling settler

indicators.note: a settler who is struggling is thrown about, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A struggling pioneer is being given a helping hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of legs and a crossbar used to hold up a table top.

clue.text: Felt slightly unhinged

definitions.meaning: made physical contact with, past tense

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both having made contact with by hand and, informally, mildly mad.

clue.text: Component widely used once for insurance

indicators.note: widely used once, a loose signal that the letters are spread about and reused in a new order

explanation.surface: Insurance products once had a component that many people relied on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widely' does two things as the setter means it, fodder and part of the signal; the blogger calls this semi all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a savings-linked life insurance plan, much used for mortgages in Britain.

clue.text: Wind starts to twirl umbrella right now

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Gusts begin to spin an umbrella around immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind a handle is to turn it round.

clue.text: In the Orient, Society that is most casual

indicators.note: In puts the society letters inside the word for the Orient

parts.note: the Orient is the East
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: In the Far East, high society is very laid-back.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy can mean relaxed and informal, so the superlative means most casual.

clue.text: One who swears on his horse?

definitions.text: One who swears on his horse?

parts.words: One who swears on his horse?
parts.note: the surface suggests someone taking an oath on a horse, but it describes a cavalryman, famous for cursing in the idiom 'swear like a ...'

explanation.surface: Someone takes an oath while sitting on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swears' looks like oath-taking; it is the cursing of the idiom about mounted soldiers, and 'on his horse' makes him cavalry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry soldier is a mounted serviceman, proverbially foul-mouthed in the phrase about swearing like one.

clue.text: I tut about charge for lessons

indicators.note: about says the letters of I tut are turned around into a new order

parts.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at the fee for lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching, the giving of lessons.

clue.text: Examination comprising some major algebra

indicators.note: comprising some says the answer is a run of letters held within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A test includes a large amount of algebra.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft made 'Examination comprising' the definition; 'comprising' belongs with 'some' as the signal, and 'Examination' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in language exams, is called by this name.

clue.text: Soldiers arresting meek people who do not use the NHS

definitions.text: people who do not use the NHS

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the soldiers enclose the meek word

parts.note: privates are ordinary soldiers
patient, meek and uncomplaining

explanation.surface: Troops detain mild-mannered people who pay for their own healthcare.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's free National Health Service; those who pay for treatment instead are private.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people who pay for medical treatment outside the state health service.

clue.text: Phone the French to begin fairy dance

parts.note: to ring is to phone
le is French for the

indicators.note: begin says only the opening letter of to is used

explanation.surface: Call the French people to start a fairy dance.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage this is a dance in a circle, as fairies were believed to perform.

clue.text: Wrongly mistreated union valuation that falls short

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the two words that follow are set out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A trade union was badly treated and its worth underrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Underrating something means putting a value on it that is too low, a valuation falling short of the truth.

clue.text: Bird submerged in bath awkwardly

indicators.note: the bird is sunk out of sight inside the phrase bath awkwardly, across the word break

explanation.surface: A bird is clumsily plunged into a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk is a bird of prey, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Half-hearted step I'd taken

indicators.note: taken here means drawn out of the words step I'd, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone took a step without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm water is tepid, and figuratively tepid support is lacking enthusiasm, half-hearted.

clue.text: Empty barrel of first-class content — it goes on the wicket

indicators.note: content means what is held inside, so the first-class letters go into the emptied barrel
an empty barrel has nothing inside, so only its outside letters remain

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A hollow cask with fine contents is placed on a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIL is one of the two small crosspieces resting on the stumps in cricket, which together form the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: A bail is a crosspiece laid across the top of the cricket stumps.

clue.text: Warm up recipe held in centre

indicators.note: held means the warming word holds the recipe letter inside

parts.note: to heat is to warm up
R is short for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Reheat a recipe kept in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre, as in the heart of the city.

clue.text: Custom of America with Georgia connection

parts.note: USA, the United States of America
GE is the international code for the country Georgia

explanation.surface: An American tradition linked to the state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, established custom.

clue.text: Most discerning river bug

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a bug is a pest, an annoying insect

explanation.surface: The sharpest critic is a river bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The deepest thinker shows most insight, so it can stand for most discerning.

clue.text: Sodium smell springing up

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A whiff of sodium is starting to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being, beginning to develop.

clue.text: Exacts former wrongs

parts.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-partner
torts are civil wrongs in law

explanation.surface: Someone takes revenge for past injuries.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact money is to demand and obtain it by force, which is to extort it.

clue.text: Made a bolt for it — ace sped away

indicators.note: away says the letters run off into a different order

explanation.surface: An ace hurried away in a bid to break free.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a bolt for it is to run off, and to have got clear is to have escaped.

clue.text: Grass harvest with nothing added is still fodder

indicators.note: added says the nothing letter is put into the fodder word

parts.note: silage is fodder stored without drying, still being animal feed
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Grass cut and kept with nothing extra stays animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is green fodder cut and fed fresh to stock, a harvest of grass.

clue.text: Cheeky young woman's belongings

definitions.meaning: a dated term for a saucy or impudent girl
luggage, the cases and bags taken on a journey

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an impudent young woman, in old-fashioned usage, and luggage carried when travelling.

clue.text: Brother, pocketing tool, became a troublemaker

indicators.note: pocketing means the brother word takes the tool inside it

parts.note: Brer is the folk form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit
an awl is a pointed tool for making holes

explanation.surface: A brother who stole a tool turned bad.
explanation.walkthrough: BRER comes from the Uncle Remus folk tales of Brer Rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawler fights noisily in public, a troublemaker.

clue.text: Recruits surprisingly listen on square

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters of listen turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: S taken as an abbreviation for square, as the blog gives it

explanation.surface: Recruits listen in surprise on the parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist someone is to recruit them, as into the army.

clue.text: Produce a whip

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a harvested yield of farm produce and a rider's short whip.

clue.text: Seat in Diana's vehicle

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A seat inside the princess's van.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low backless sofa, a type of seat.

clue.text: Medicine for Phil and Lily oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly says to take the first, third and other odd-placed letters of each name

explanation.surface: Some medicine for a couple named Phil and Lily, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a tablet of medicine.

clue.text: Scholar went to Long Island locality east of Java

parts.note: BA, a Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A scholar travels to Long Island, then a place east of Java.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is the Indonesian island lying just east of Java.

clue.text: One knight uproots the flower

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: uproots, in a down clue, turns the knight's title upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A lone knight pulls up the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden flower with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Ample librarians may become leading ladies

indicators.note: may become says the letters can be turned into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Well-built library staff might one day star on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal female dancers of a ballet company are its leading ladies.

clue.text: I'd eat my stew between dawn and dusk

indicators.note: stew says the letters are stirred up together like a stew

explanation.surface: Someone plans to eat a stew during the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight hours run from dawn until dusk.

clue.text: Checks siblings about moving ahead

indicators.note: moving ahead says that flipped pair is taken out and set at the front of the word
about here means turned around, so the pair of letters near the end of the siblings word is flipped

parts.note: sisters are female siblings

explanation.surface: Someone stops their sisters from going forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the ER of SISTERS round to RE (SISTRES); 'moving ahead' puts that RE first, giving RE + SISTS. The blogger finds this loose, with 'moving' half doing double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an attack is to hold it back, which is to resist it.
